summary: The complete maintained inventory exposed an October 6 Cloud Service Description change. Four provider-scoped Machine Data Lake records were added without generalizing availability, entitlement or authorization. Automated validation passed, but publication is held because the supported browser surface timed out before fresh affected-route, native PDF and independently reopened HTML checks could be completed.

screenPdfHtmlWebMcpAgreement.detail: Automated page, print and existing read-only WebMCP reports agree on the four records and citations. Screen/native PDF/independently reopened HTML agreement is not certified.

liveBaselineDiagnostic.detail: Two diagnostics from the exact currently deployed Sites source confirmed real D1 readiness, revision content-6dcf491dfeb864140adc2937, engine-c5ff569aec1b2f034270, exact 668-record manifest/bundle integrity and bounded queries. Both timed out on the read-only API method-guard check; the first confirmed all seven fallback adapters, while the retry also timed out during fallback retrieval. These are actual failed checks, not passes, and add a transient live-delivery follow-up without changing the candidate's publication hold.

publication.detail: No GitHub-main or Sites publication is claimed. The prior complete live revision remains active because applicable browser and export verification is incomplete.

soak.detail: check-soak holds advancement on browser journeys, themes/narrow screens, keyboard, HTML reopen, PDF rendering and live revision for this changed candidate. The 72-hour observation window is not being used as a delay.

recommendations: Retry the supported rendered-browser service, then exercise AWS commercial, both GovCloud regimes, GCP, Azure, provider-only, region-only, invalid and mismatched selections in default and Cisco themes.
Capture a native PDF page by page and independently reopen the exact saved HTML; compare route, four Machine Data Lake rows, citations and immutable revision with screen and read-only WebMCP.

Retry the live read-only API guard and fallback diagnostic from the matching deployed source; publish only after affected-content checks pass, retaining the current complete revision and rollback boundary until then.
